subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core session-auth PIN gate, and if so should it be a SecretRef-backed config/session-state primitive or a plugin/trusted-policy pattern?
rationale: Automation can prove the source gap, but cannot choose the product and security boundary because the feature affects fail-closed tool execution, secret handling, session reset state, prompt-injection protection, and user recovery behavior.

options.title: Design a core primitive
options.body: Add a narrow core session-auth design with SecretRef-backed secret material, trusted verifier command/tool or native command, authenticated session state, reset clearing, docs, and focused security tests.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned
options.body: Document how an explicitly trusted plugin policy can implement the gate today, and keep core limited to generic session state and before-tool-call APIs unless a missing seam is identified.

options.title: Fold into guardrail API work
options.body: Defer the PIN-specific shape until broader guardrail/approval API decisions settle the standard action-blocking boundary.

recommendation.title: Design a core primitive
recommendation.body: Add a narrow core session-auth design with SecretRef-backed secret material, trusted verifier command/tool or native command, authenticated session state, reset clearing, docs, and focused security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined signal from current central-file history, adjacent plugin/Gateway PR history, and issue-timeline mentions for this product/security boundary.
